note: A continuously refreshed coding benchmark, the working model for contamination free evaluation.
title: LiveCodeBench: Holistic and Contamination Free Evaluation of Large Language Models for Code

reading.body:
LiveCodeBench is a continuously refreshed coding benchmark, built specifically to prevent the contamination problem where a model has already seen the test questions during training.

Continuous refresh is the key design choice, and it directly addresses a problem named explicitly elsewhere in this collection, the position paper calling for per-benchmark contamination measurement. A benchmark that adds new problems on an ongoing basis cannot be memorized in advance the way a static, published benchmark can, which makes its scores harder to game and more informative about genuine capability.

The paper does not claim to solve contamination for benchmarks other than coding tasks, and does not report how its refresh rate compares to how quickly frontier models are trained and released.

explain_beginner: Researchers created LiveCodeBench, a new way to test how well AI language models can write code. Unlike older tests that stay the same, this benchmark continuously adds fresh coding problems from real programming competitions, preventing models from memorizing answers. The system checks not just code generation but also whether models can fix their own mistakes and predict what code will output. Testing 52 different models revealed that older benchmarks may give inflated scores because models have seen similar problems before.
explain_business: Organizations selecting LLMs for coding tasks need accurate, unbiased performance metrics. LiveCodeBench provides confidence that model evaluations reflect genuine capabilities rather than memorization by continuously introducing fresh problems from actual competitions. This enables better purchasing decisions and realistic expectations for deployment. The ongoing refresh cycle means evaluations remain valid over time, reducing risk of selecting models that overperformed on outdated benchmarks but underperform in production.
explain_practitioner: LiveCodeBench addresses benchmark contamination by dynamically sourcing problems from LeetCode, AtCoder, and CodeForces published after May 2023, ensuring evaluation data hasn't been seen during model training. The framework evaluates 52 LLMs across code generation and auxiliary capabilities including self-repair, execution, and test output prediction. The study demonstrates evidence of overfitting to existing static benchmarks and provides comprehensive empirical analysis of 18 base and 34 instruction-tuned models. Researchers will release all prompts, completions, and a toolkit for community extension.
